before: std::string_view stores a pointer and length, not an owning string copy. Its owner must remain alive and its storage must remain valid while the view is used.

Assigning owner[0] changes an existing character without reallocating storage. The view sees that edit. Operations that replace or grow the owner may invalidate the view; do not keep a view into a destroyed temporary string.

remove_prefix shortens the view, not the owning string. It requires that the removed count is no greater than the view length. A string_view also need not end with a null character; data() is not automatically a C-string.

Expected output or behavior: Forest
orest Forest. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Make an owning std::string copy from the view and compare what later owner edits affect. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: std::string_view remembers where text starts and how many character units it covers. It does not own or copy that text. The owning string must keep its storage alive while the view uses it.
Changing an existing character in owner changes the text the view reads. This character assignment does not move the string's storage, so the view remains valid here.
remove_prefix(1) moves the view's start forward by one character unit. It does not erase anything from owner. The count removed must not exceed the view's length.
The program prints Forest, then orest Forest on the next line. The view sees the capital F. Removing its prefix hides that first character only from the view.

Destroying the owner, or an operation that moves its storage, can invalidate the view. Also, a view need not end at a null character, the marker used to end a C-style string. Its data() pointer alone is not a promise of that ending.
